dish.title: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
dish.description: Soy-and-cumin-marinated sirloin strips seared hard in a smoking-hot skillet, tossed with charred red onion, juicy tomato wedges, garlic, and a fruity ají amarillo-vinegar-soy sauce, finished with cilantro and folded with crisp oven fries; served with white rice.

recipe_version.title: Peruvian Lomo Saltado
recipe_version.description: Soy-and-cumin-marinated sirloin strips seared hard in a smoking-hot skillet, tossed with charred red onion, juicy tomato wedges, garlic, and a fruity ají amarillo-vinegar-soy sauce, finished with cilantro and folded with crisp oven fries; served with white rice.

ingredients.name: top sirloin steak
ingredients.preparation: cut across the grain into strips 1/2 inch thick and 2 inches long

ingredients.name: soy sauce
ingredients.note: 2 tbsp marinade, 2 tbsp sauce. Soy and wheat.

ingredients.name: ají amarillo paste
ingredients.display_name: ají amarillo paste (Peruvian yellow chile paste)
ingredients.note: Contract: plain jarred ají amarillo pepper paste (peppers, water, salt, acid). Not huancaína or other ají sauces that contain cheese, milk, or crackers. Latin aisle, Latin market, or online.

ingredients.name: garlic
ingredients.note: 2 for the marinade, 3 for the stir-fry

ingredients.name: Roma tomatoes
ingredients.preparation: each cut lengthwise into 6 wedges, seeds scooped out

ingredients.name: frozen French fries
ingredients.note: Contract: plain fries (potatoes, oil, salt; dextrose is fine). No seasoned, battered, or coated fries.

ingredients.name: neutral oil
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp per beef batch, 1 tbsp for the onions

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: 3/4 tsp for the rice, the rest to taste at the end

steps.title: Heat the oven and marinate the beef
steps.body: Heat the oven to 425°F (or the temperature on your fry package, 425 to 450°F); it preheats during the 15 minutes of prep (overlap stated). Toss the beef strips with 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 cloves minced garlic, the cumin, and the pepper; let it marinate while you prep.

steps.title: Prep the vegetables, sauce, and rice
steps.body: Cut the onion into 1/2-inch wedges and separate the layers. Cut the tomatoes into seeded wedges. Mince the remaining 3 garlic cloves. Chop the cilantro. Rinse the rice. In a small bowl stir together 2 tbsp soy sauce, the red wine vinegar, and the ají amarillo paste (the sauce).

steps.title: Start the fries and rice
steps.body: Spread the frozen fries in a single layer on a rimmed sheet pan and bake 22 to 25 minutes, flipping once halfway, until deep golden and crisp. At the same time bring the rice, 2 1/4 cups water, and 3/4 tsp salt to a boil in a 2-quart saucepan, cover, reduce to low, and cook 15 minutes; then keep covered off the heat. Both are hands-off; flip the fries at about minute 12.

steps.title: Sear the beef
steps.body: About 13 minutes after the fries go in, heat a 12-inch carbon-steel or cast-iron skillet (or wok) over high until smoking, about 2 minutes. Add 1 tbsp oil and half the beef in a single layer; sear undisturbed 1 minute, then toss 30 to 60 seconds until browned outside and still pink inside. Transfer to a plate. Repeat with 1 tbsp oil and the rest of the beef.

steps.title: Char the onion and garlic
steps.body: Add the last 1 tbsp oil and the onion. Stir-fry over high 90 seconds, until the edges char but the onion is still crisp. Add the garlic and toss 15 seconds.

steps.title: Tomatoes, sauce, and beef
steps.body: Add the tomatoes and toss 45 seconds just to warm them. Pour the sauce around the edge of the pan so it sizzles and reduces, about 20 seconds. Return the beef and its juices and toss 30 seconds. Off heat, add most of the cilantro; taste and add salt only if needed (the soy is salty).

steps.title: Plate
steps.body: Fold about one-third of the hot fries into the skillet so they soak up some sauce; pile the rest alongside. Pack rice into a small cup and unmold a dome onto each plate. Spoon the lomo saltado next to the rice with its juices, add the remaining fries, and scatter the remaining cilantro. Serve at once while the fries are crisp. kitchen_tested is false.

equipment: 12-inch carbon-steel or cast-iron skillet or wok
recipe_version.heat: 425°F oven for fries (preheat overlaps prep); rice high then low; skillet on high, smoking hot, for the stir-fry.
recipe_version.doneness: Beef browned outside, pink and juicy inside (about medium). Onion edges charred but crisp. Tomatoes warmed, not collapsed. Fries deep golden and crisp. Rice fluffy. kitchen_tested is false.

coverage_contribution: Peruvian 0->1; unique fries-plus-wok format; beef only grilled flank + tibs. Adventurous because of ají amarillo paste sourcing, not culture.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with Ethiopian Beef Tibs: fast-seared beef with onion, but a soy-vinegar-ají amarillo sauce, tomatoes, and fries instead of berbere. Compared with Gochujang Grilled Flank Steak: beef, but wok-seared strips, not a grilled steak. Not a live-catalog duplicate.
deliberately_not: Not Ethiopian tibs twin (different sauce/method), not a Chinese beef-and-broccoli.
selection_alignment: Matches WAVE.json/selection.json identity: peruvian · stir-fry · beef sirloin · hh001_intent false -> hh001_eligible false. Selection time band 30–45; written clock 40 minutes. Classification deviations from proposal: effort_level moderate (WAVE proposal) -> involved (rubric).

specialty_items: ají amarillo paste (specialty-store likely, no true substitute)

rationale.effort: Steady prep (1); high-heat batch stir-fry is continuous (2); stir-fry, oven fries, and rice must converge hot at the plate (2); batch searing, timing-sensitive (1); oven, rice pot, and skillet in parallel (1). Sum 7 -> involved. WAVE proposed moderate; the third coordinated component (fries) is what pushes past the tibs / thai-basil precedent (5, moderate).
rationale.complexity: 11 countable (1). Ají amarillo paste is the namesake flavor, specialty-store likely and with no true substitute (2, scored once; sourcing not double-counted, parity with Thai basil). Marinade plus pan sauce (1). Sum 4 -> adventurous, driven only by ají amarillo availability, not by Peruvian cuisine.

classification.cultural_bias_guardrail: Cuisine unfamiliarity adds no points; specialty-store items scored once under specialty_burden, pantry_familiarity kept 0 (r2 convention).
